findings.reason: without a control (for example permuting the per-loop sign/geometry assignment, or fitting a parallel path with the saddle loops removed) the node's whole measure rests on a held-out residual that can improve for reasons other than the saddle loops resolving n, so the gate cannot show its guard fires.
findings.text: the §5 done-when ("saddle-loop predictions ... reproduce vacuum shots held out of the fit") carries no declared negative control, unlike §4's permuted-drive control

findings.reason: the traversal sign is explicitly allowed to end "undecided" and the tail width is a deliverable owed to a donor plan, so the node has no single pass/fail outcome and cannot be reviewed or closed on one verdict.
findings.text: §5 bundles four deliverables to close on one verdict: admission of the 36 saddle loops into the constraint set, per-loop traversal-sign promotion-or-undecided, the n = 1–6 P4/P5 harmonic re-measure, and the localised-tail width owed to `mast-misfit-toroidal-harmonics`

findings.reason: the same URL is used by peer plans (`mast-catalog-geometry-recovery.html`) and the document is reachable through the Resources panel built from parsed state, so this is a stale href rather than a missing document, and correcting it does not change what a node builds.

findings.reason: the done-when claims grouped resistances "improve held-out transient residuals", which is only meaningful if the drive amplitude/turn semantics are grounded; otherwise a held-out improvement can come from a mis-scaled drive rather than a real resistance, and the node is sent at the wrong mechanism, so the plan should state how the driven-cohort excitation is grounded (measured amplitude, or a bound carried as uncertainty).
findings.text: §4 extends the free-decay resistance fit to "driven ramps and switch-offs", but the cited module states in its own docstring "Turn counts do not enter. The initial condition is fitted per shot rather than propagated from the drive", and `mast_fitted_parameters.py` records the published ampere-turn semantics as still unconfirmed by the `VERTICAL_PAIR_EXPLAINED` negative result; a driven-transient fit requires the drive, so the same ungrounded amplitude that the free-decay method sidestepped is reintroduced into the fit
